lines.text: Later it cools off. Somebody will still say 'it was so nice earlier.' As if that helps.
Later it cools off. Time to find out who really 'runs warm.'
Later it cools off. I could make that sound dramatic, but I'm not a news channel.
Later it cools off. Every phone will report it like a scoop. I said it first.
Later it cools off. Every 'it's warmer than it looks' turns into 'it's colder than it looks.'
Later it cools off. The ice cream trucks are working against the clock.
Later it cools off. I'd say it louder, but this is my only font size.
Later it cools off. I'd sugarcoat it, but I only come in black and white.
Later it cools off. Every dog walker in town is about to walk faster.
Later it cools off. Somewhere a meteorologist is pretending that was hard to see.
Later it cools off. Sleeves get pulled down over hands all over town.
Later it cools off. Most people out there dressed for the good part. Optimists.
Later it cools off. Restaurant patios start handing out blankets.
Later it cools off. Goosebumps all around. I'm exempt.
Now: 'Lovely out.' Later: 'Since when is it this cold?'
Warm in the middle, cold at both ends. Like a microwaved burrito.
Warm for a while, then cool again. Every office in town fights over the window twice.
Warm, then cool again. The 'always dress in layers' crowd gets to be smug today. I'm smug every day.
It warms up, then cools back down. Lost-and-found bins love days like this.
Warm for a bit, then cool again. At any moment, half the town is dressed wrong.
It warms up, then cools again. Every grandma who said 'take something warm' wins today.
Warm, then cool again. Don't like the weather? Wait. Like it? Also wait.
Warm for a bit, then cool again. Finally, the vest people have their day.
Warm, then cool again. I'd call it unpredictable, but I predicted it.
It warms up, then cools back down. The weather's going for 'something for everyone.' Nobody asked.
Layer on, layer off, layer on again. Today's weather is doing the Hokey Pokey.
Warm, then cool again. A rough day to look effortless. I manage.
Warm for a bit, then cool again. I can't promise it's nice. I can promise it's both.
It warms up, then cools again. Somebody will announce 'it's so nice out' just before it isn't.
Cold. No, warm. Actually, cold. The weather's holding up the line.
Perfect weather. 'Just in case' layers everywhere, needed by no one.
Perfect weather. Everyone suddenly cares about vitamin D.
Perfect weather out there, I'm told. I don't get a window.
Perfect weather. Every runner in town is out, making sure everyone notices.
Perfect weather. Whatever goes wrong today, the weather has an alibi.
Perfect weather. Good moods everywhere. It's exhausting to watch.
Perfect weather. I'd glow, but e-ink doesn't glow.
Perfect weather. Somewhere an outdoor wedding is getting away with it.
Forecast: flawless. Like me. I'm allowed to say it, it's my screen.
Later it warms up. Turns out the early bird just gets the cold.
Later it warms up. Whoever wore shorts at the start finally looks like a genius.
Later it warms up. The day's a slow starter. I respect that. Actually, no, I don't.
Later it warms up. So all the early complaining was for nothing. Again.
Later it warms up. The day gets a redemption arc. I never needed one.
Later it warms up. Every bag in town gets one layer heavier.
Later it warms up. Nobody believes that at first. Then everyone acts like they knew.
Later it warms up. Even the pigeons look less offended by then.
Later it warms up. The lighter outfit's already drawn. Looks great on e-ink.
Later it warms up. Fashionably late, the weather. I'm never late. I'm never anywhere.
Later it warms up. Car heaters at first, AC by the end. Nobody's happy.
Later it warms up. Ladies and gentlemen, the layer has left the building.
Rain. Every store in town is putting down the soggy cardboard.
Raining, and the umbrella sellers appear out of thin air. Faster than me, even.
Rain. Somewhere a bus is lining up the big puddle.
Raining. A day for staying in. I've trained my whole life for this.
Rain. Everybody who said 'it won't rain' has gone very quiet.
Rain. Every ride app just raised its prices. Coincidence, I'm sure.
Rain. Somebody will say 'nice weather for ducks.' The ducks didn't ask.
Rain. It always gets heavier the second someone steps outside. I've checked.
Rain. Somewhere a picnic is being renamed 'indoor picnic.'
Rain. All those rain boots finally pay for themselves.
Rain. Everyone does the little jog to the door, as if it helps.
Wet sidewalks, wet dogs, wet socks. I'm the only dry thing in this sentence.
Cool out. Not cold enough to complain about. People will try anyway.
Cool out. The iced coffee people start lying about being fine.
Cool out. Perfect operating temperature for me. Not that anyone asked.
Cool out. Coffee becomes a hand warmer you can sip.
Cool out. The weather's fine. I'm excellent. We don't compare.
Cool out. Dogs in little sweaters everywhere. Finally, some competition.
Cool out. Hands in pockets everywhere. Everyone looks a little guilty.
Cool out. The yearly 'is it too early for soup?' debate is open.
Cool out. I rate it one jacket out of one jacket.
